title: Interface lemmas behind CompCert's transf_c_program_correct
intent: Assemble CompCert's headline correctness theorem — a successfully compiled C program is related to its assembly by a backward simulation — in one line from two interface lemmas (transf_c_program_match, c_semantic_preservation), so the client never unfolds the 20-pass compile chain or the simulation construction.

parent.name: transf_c_program_correct
parent.statement:
Theorem transf_c_program_correct:
  forall p tp,
  transf_c_program p = OK tp ->
  backward_simulation (Csem.semantics p) (Asm.semantics tp).

children.name: transf_c_program_match
children.statement:
Theorem transf_c_program_match:
  forall p tp,
  transf_c_program p = OK tp ->
  match_prog p tp.
children.closed_by: unfold transf_c_program and each pass, then exists pi; split. apply <pass>proof.transf_program_match for all 20 passes, ending reflexivity (lines 269-318)

children.name: c_semantic_preservation
children.statement:
Theorem c_semantic_preservation:
  forall p tp,
  match_prog p tp ->
  backward_simulation (Csem.semantics p) (Asm.semantics tp).
children.closed_by: compose_backward_simulation with atomic (Cstrategy.semantics p), factor_backward_simulation, Cstrategy.strategy_simulation, and proj2 (cstrategy_semantic_preservation _ _ H) (lines 423-432)

applicability.goal_shape: Theorem whose conclusion is the conclusion of one named lemma and whose hypothesis is the hypothesis of another, so the proof is a chain of apply over interface lemmas (A -> B -> C proved as apply l2; apply l1)
applicability.use_when: the goal is exactly a composition of two already-proved facts stated at an abstraction boundary, and unfolding the underlying definition would be long or would repeat work the lemmas already package (here transf_c_program and match_prog)
applicability.avoid_when: the children's statements do not line up (the apply must leave no residual obligation); or the boundary lemma is not self-contained enough for a client to use without further unfolding

claims.claim: The parent transf_c_program_correct closes in a single tactic line, apply c_semantic_preservation; apply transf_c_program_match; auto, without unfolding transf_c_program or match_prog.
claims.evidence: https://github.com/AbsInt/CompCert/blob/2685140bf72c959446981fb99b5e44a8975021bc/driver/Compiler.v#L446-L452 (the parent excerpt is the statement plus Proof. / the one apply line / Qed.)

claims.claim: The authors describe the plan in the comment above the theorem: 'Combining the results above, we obtain semantic preservation for two usage scenarios of CompCert: compilation of a single monolithic program, and separate compilation of multiple source files followed by linking.'

The main proof is 1 glue line applying 2 lemmas, and the two children's proofs are 50 and 10 lines (direct_lemmas = 2, glue_lines = 1, child_lines = [50, 10], depth = 2), counted over driver/Compiler.v lines 446-452, 265-318 and 419-432.
The same two interface lemmas are reused at a second call site: separate_transf_c_program_correct applies transf_c_program_match (line 476) and c_semantic_preservation (line 480).

c_semantic_preservation closes by applying proj2 (cstrategy_semantic_preservation _ _ H) (line 431), so the chain of project lemmas below the main theorem reaches depth 2: transf_c_program_correct -> c_semantic_preservation -> cstrategy_semantic_preservation, all in driver/Compiler.v.

metrics.how_counted: glue = line 451 of driver/Compiler.v (the single tactic line); child proofs = lines 269-318 (transf_c_program_match) and 423-432 (c_semantic_preservation), counted Proof. through Qed.; depth = the chain transf_c_program_correct -> c_semantic_preservation -> cstrategy_semantic_preservation, all in driver/Compiler.v

consequences: The glue is nothing but apply, so the decomposition's only obligation is that the children's statements line up exactly: transf_c_program_match must end in match_prog and c_semantic_preservation must take match_prog, or the two applies will not compose. Each child then carries the real work — transf_c_program_match proves the 20-pass chain to match_prog and c_semantic_preservation builds the backward simulation — so a reader who wants the argument must descend into those bodies and then into the per-pass proof files. Failure mode: if a pass is added or removed, transf_c_program_match's body must be updated by hand to stay in sync with transf_c_program, while the parent and c_semantic_preservation never change.
